name: Pearly Purple
lede: Pearly Purple is a dusty, medium-dark magenta-purple filed under nature words, closest in our library to the redder, deeper Mulberry.

sections.title: A pearl word, not a pearl color
sections.body:
Our classifier files Pearly Purple's name as a nature word, built on "pearly," the family ColorHub uses for plant, animal, food and landscape terms [1]. It is not literally the color of a pearl: pearls run pale and iridescent, while this purple sits at lightness 55 and a fairly strong chroma of 43 on the LCH scale [1]. Wikipedia's color list is the only source we hold for the name, and it does not explain who coined it or when [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[cattleya]], [[mulberry-crayola]], [[pale-magenta]] and [[mathews-purple]], at 5.1, 5.9, 6 and 6.3 ΔE [1]. Both sit in the *Purples* family, but Mulberry reads redder and a little darker [1]. Munsell plots the hue near 0.7RP, between red-purple and plain purple [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, has no painting where Pearly Purple covers at least five percent of the canvas within six CIEDE2000 units [2]. That absence is itself a finding: this is a screen-list color, not one the paint record of Western and Asian museum paintings happens to reach [2]. As with any hex value, the swatch here is a screen approximation, not a measured pigment [1].
